Here’s an advanced Keras project that pushes well beyond typical models—tailored to your 50 years of ML/AI experience. It leverages multi-modal inputs and multi-task learning using the Functional API, combining image, numerical, and categorical data to perform both regression and classification. Use cases include real-world scenarios like medical diagnosis (image + vitals → disease detection + severity score) or property assessment (house image + features → price + condition score).

Project Title

ai-ml-ds-PqZrTyXgWu

PropertyConditionEstimator
Filename: property_condition_estimator.py

📌 Short Description

A multi-input, multi-output Keras model that takes in house images, numerical features (area, age), and categorical features (type, location), then simultaneously predicts property price (regression) and condition score (classification). Advanced use of shared layers, embeddings, and weighted loss handling.

🛠️ Python Code

# property_condition_estimator.py
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from typing import List
from tensorflow import keras
from tensorflow.keras import layers
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

# 1. Load dataset (example from sklearn for placeholders)
from tensorflow.keras.datasets import cifar10
(x_img: np.ndarray, y_cls: np.ndarray), _ = cifar10.load_data()

# Placeholder numeric/categorical synthetic data
num_samples: int = x_img.shape[0]
num_feats: np.ndarray = np.random.rand(num_samples, 2)  # e.g. [area, age]
cat_feats: np.ndarray = np.random.randint(0, 5, size=(num_samples,))  # e.g. 5 location types

price_true: np.ndarray = np.random.rand(num_samples, 1) * 500_000  # house price
cond_true: np.ndarray = np.random.randint(0, 3, size=(num_samples,))  # condition score 0-2

# Split
X_img_train, X_img_val, num_train, num_val, cat_train, cat_val, y_price_train, y_price_val, y_cond_train, y_cond_val = train_test_split(
    x_img, num_feats, cat_feats, price_true, cond_true, test_size=0.2, random_state=42)

# Preprocess numerical features
scaler: StandardScaler = StandardScaler()
num_train: np.ndarray = scaler.fit_transform(num_train)
num_val: np.ndarray = scaler.transform(num_val)

# One-hot encode condition target
y_cond_train_oh: np.ndarray = keras.utils.to_categorical(y_cond_train, num_classes=3)
y_cond_val_oh: np.ndarray = keras.utils.to_categorical(y_cond_val, num_classes=3)

# 2. Build model
img_input = layers.Input(shape=(32,32,3), name="img_input")
x_img = layers.Conv2D(32,3,activation="relu")(img_input)
x_img = layers.MaxPooling2D()(x_img)
x_img = layers.Conv2D(64,3,activation="relu")(x_img)
x_img = layers.Flatten()(x_img)

num_input = layers.Input(shape=(2,), name="num_input")
x_num = layers.Dense(16, activation="relu")(num_input)

cat_input = layers.Input(shape=(1,), name="cat_input")
x_cat = layers.Embedding(input_dim=5, output_dim=3, input_length=1)(cat_input)
x_cat = layers.Flatten()(x_cat)

# Merge
merged = layers.concatenate([x_img, x_num, x_cat])
shared = layers.Dense(128, activation="relu")(merged)
shared = layers.Dropout(0.3)(shared)

# Two outputs
price_out = layers.Dense(1, name="price_output")(shared)
cond_out = layers.Dense(3, activation="softmax", name="cond_output")(shared)

model = keras.Model(inputs=[img_input, num_input, cat_input], outputs=[price_out, cond_out])

# Compile
model.compile(
    optimizer="adam",
    loss={"price_output": "mse", "cond_output": "categorical_crossentropy"},
    loss_weights={"price_output": 1.0, "cond_output": 0.5},
    metrics={"price_output": keras.metrics.RootMeanSquaredError(), "cond_output": "accuracy"},
)

model.summary()

# 3. Train
history = model.fit(
    {"img_input": X_img_train, "num_input": num_train, "cat_input": cat_train},
    {"price_output": y_price_train, "cond_output": y_cond_train_oh},
    validation_data=(
        {"img_input": X_img_val, "num_input": num_val, "cat_input": cat_val},
        {"price_output": y_price_val, "cond_output": y_cond_val_oh},
    ),
    epochs=10,
    batch_size=64
)

# 4. Usage examples
pred_price, pred_cond = model.predict({
    "img_input": X_img_val[:2],
    "num_input": num_val[:2],
    "cat_input": cat_val[:2]
})
for i, (p, c) in enumerate(zip(pred_price, pred_cond)):
    print(f"Sample {i}: Price ≈ ${p[0]:.2f}, Condition class = {np.argmax(c)}")

🧠 Project Title

ai-ml-ds-VuXyZpAbCd
Filename: multi_modal_attention_estimator.py

🔍 Short Description

Build a multi-input Keras model combining image, time-series, and text data. It uses convolutional backbones, transformer encoders, and cross-modal attention to predict both a continuous target (e.g. future price trend) and a classification target (e.g. risk level).

🧩 Full Python Code

# multi_modal_attention_estimator.py
import numpy as np
import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow import keras
from tensorflow.keras import layers
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

# 1. Simulated multimodal data (replace with real dataset)
n: int = 1000
img_data: np.ndarray = np.random.rand(n, 64, 64, 3).astype('float32')
ts_data: np.ndarray = np.random.rand(n, 10, 5).astype('float32')  # 10 time steps, 5 features
txt_data: np.ndarray = np.random.randint(1, 5000, size=(n, 20))    # tokenized text seq = 20
y_reg: np.ndarray = np.random.rand(n,1)*1000
y_clf: np.ndarray = np.random.randint(0,4, size=(n,))

# Train/val split
(Xi, Xi_val, Xts, Xts_val, Xt, Xt_val, yR, yR_val, yC, yC_val) = train_test_split(
    img_data, ts_data, txt_data, y_reg, y_clf, test_size=0.2, random_state=42)

# Preprocess time-series scaler
scaler_ts = StandardScaler()
Xts = scaler_ts.fit_transform(Xts.reshape(-1, Xts.shape[-1])).reshape(Xts.shape)
Xts_val = scaler_ts.transform(Xts_val.reshape(-1, Xts_val.shape[-1])).reshape(Xts_val.shape)

# One‑hot classification labels
yC_oh = keras.utils.to_categorical(yC, num_classes=4)
yC_val_oh = keras.utils.to_categorical(yC_val, num_classes=4)

# 2. Model definition
## 2.1 Image branch
img_input = layers.Input(shape=(64,64,3), name='img_input')
x1 = layers.Conv2D(32,3,activation='relu')(img_input)
x1 = layers.MaxPool2D()(x1)
x1 = layers.Conv2D(64,3,activation='relu')(x1)
x1 = layers.GlobalAveragePooling2D()(x1)

## 2.2 Time‑series branch + transformer encoder
ts_input = layers.Input(shape=(10,5), name='ts_input')
x2 = layers.MultiHeadAttention(num_heads=4, key_dim=8)(ts_input, ts_input)
x2 = layers.LayerNormalization()(x2 + ts_input)
x2 = layers.GlobalAveragePooling1D()(x2)

## 2.3 Text branch with embedding + transformer encoder layer
txt_input = layers.Input(shape=(20,), name='txt_input')
x3 = layers.Embedding(input_dim=5000, output_dim=64)(txt_input)
x3_pos = layers.Add()([x3, tf.range(start=0, limit=20)[None,:,None]])
x3 = layers.MultiHeadAttention(num_heads=4, key_dim=16)(x3_pos, x3_pos)
x3 = layers.LayerNormalization()(x3 + x3_pos)
x3 = layers.GlobalAveragePooling1D()(x3)

# 2.4 Cross-modal attention
combined = layers.Concatenate()([x1, x2, x3])
dense = layers.Dense(256, activation='relu')(combined)
# Attention
att_scores = layers.Dense(3, activation='softmax')(dense)    # scores for x1,x2,x3
x_att = layers.Dot(axes=1)([att_scores, tf.stack([x1, x2, x3], axis=1)])
x_shared = layers.Dense(128, activation='relu')(x_att)

# 2.5 Dual outputs
out_reg = layers.Dense(1, name='price_trend')(x_shared)
out_clf = layers.Dense(4, activation='softmax', name='risk_level')(x_shared)

model = keras.Model(inputs=[img_input, ts_input, txt_input], outputs=[out_reg, out_clf])
model.compile(optimizer='adam',
              loss={'price_trend': 'mse', 'risk_level': 'categorical_crossentropy'},
              loss_weights={'price_trend': 1.0, 'risk_level': 0.7},
              metrics={'price_trend': keras.metrics.MeanAbsoluteError(),
                       'risk_level': 'accuracy'})

# 3. Train
model.fit({'img_input': Xi, 'ts_input': Xts, 'txt_input': Xt},
          {'price_trend': yR, 'risk_level': yC_oh},
          validation_data=({'img_input': Xi_val, 'ts_input': Xts_val, 'txt_input': Xt_val},
                           {'price_trend': yR_val, 'risk_level': yC_val_oh}),
          epochs=15, batch_size=32)

# 4. Example predictions
predR, predC = model.predict({'img_input': Xi_val[:2], 'ts_input': Xts_val[:2], 'txt_input': Xt_val[:2]})
for i in range(2):
    print(f"Sample {i}: PredTrend={predR[i,0]:.2f}, RiskLvl={np.argmax(predC[i])}")
